q2-177.n: Righteousness is not outward show but faith, giving, keeping promises and patience in hardship.

q2-197.n: The best provision for life's journey is mindfulness of Allah, a provision that never runs out.

q2-208.n: Islam is a whole; peace with oneself and others is part of it.

q2-222.n: Allah loves those who repent, who return each time they slip, not only those who never slip.

q2-255.n: The Verse of the Throne: Allah never sleeps and guarding all things does not tire Him; it calms the fearful and anxious.

q2-261.n: Giving is multiplied by Allah far beyond human calculation.

q2-264.n: Reminders of favours and hurtful words spoil a kindness; give without reminding people of it.

q2-282.n: Writing debts down, even between relatives and friends, protects the relationship rather than doubting trust.

q2-284.n: Allah knows what is in hearts; the verses after it ease this: Allah burdens no soul beyond its capacity.

q3-14.n: Love of wealth, spouses and children is built into human nature; it is to be ordered, not denied.

q3-31.n: True love of Allah shows in following the Prophet; its reward is Allah's love and forgiveness.

q3-92.n: The highest giving is from what you love, not from what is left over.

q3-110.n: Being the best community depends on enjoining good and forbidding wrong; it is not a birthright.

q3-133.n: A call to hasten: delaying repentance and good deeds wastes chances.

q3-146.n: Believers throughout history faced what you face and did not weaken or give in; Allah loves the patient.

q3-154.n: After distress comes calm; even in the hardest moments Allah sends security down on hearts.

q3-186.n: Hurt from people is an expected part of the road; patience and mindfulness of Allah are the mark of resolve.

q3-190.n: Reflecting on creation puts worries in proportion and strengthens faith.

q4-9.n: Fear for one's children is answered by justice and sound words today, not by worry alone.

q4-34.n: Guardianship is responsibility and provision, not domination; it is read with the verses on kindness and the hadith forbidding harm. For its legal details, consult scholars.

q4-79.n: Good comes from Allah; harm calls for self-review rather than blaming others.

q4-85.n: Interceding for good gives you a share of it; interceding for harm gives you a share of its burden.

q4-104.n: If you are in pain, so are others; the difference is hope in Allah.

q4-123.n: Wishes alone are not enough; it is deeds that a person is held to.

q4-149.n: Pardoning when able is an attribute of Allah; the verse before it allows the wronged to speak out.

q5-32.n: One life is worth all of humanity, and your own life is among them.

q5-54.n: Among those Allah loves: they do not fear the blame of any critic; a cure for people-pleasing.

q5-87.n: Strictly denying oneself what is lawful is not piety; balance is part of the religion.

q5-105.n: Your first responsibility is yourself; another's error does not harm you if you are guided and do your part.

q6-59.n: The unseen is with Allah; worry about the future eases when you recall that not a leaf falls without His knowledge.

q6-70.n: Leave gatherings that mock religion without confrontation, and remind calmly.

q6-108.n: Even in disagreement over belief there is no place for insults; insults invite worse in return.

q6-151.n: Fear of poverty does not justify wronging children; provision is guaranteed by Allah.

q7-31.n: Moderation in eating and spending is a rule of health, finance and faith.

q7-55.n: Humble, quiet prayer is closer to the heart and further from showing off.

q7-201.n: When whispering or a surge of anger strikes, remembering Allah restores clear sight.

q8-2.n: Signs of living faith: a heart that is moved, faith that grows, and reliance on Allah.

q8-28.n: Wealth and children are a test; passing it lies in balance, not attachment.

q8-61.n: If the other side inclines to peace, accept it and rely on Allah.

q9-91.n: There is no blame on the weak, the sick or those without means if they are sincere; their excuse is accepted.

q9-119.n: Truthful company protects you; choose friends from among the truthful.

q10-44.n: Allah wrongs no one; reviewing oneself comes before blaming fate.

q10-107.n: Harm and good are in Allah's hand; do not attach your fear or hope to anyone else.

q11-61.n: People are placed on earth to build it up; useful work is worship.

q11-123.n: All matters belong to Allah; worship Him, rely on Him, and let go of what you cannot control.

q12-64.n: Said by Ya‘qub as he sent his son after losing Yusuf: when afraid for one's children, entrust their safety to Allah.

q12-83.n: Beautiful patience does not exclude hope: Ya‘qub was patient while hoping to be reunited.

q12-111.n: The prophets' stories are not tales but lessons for situations like ours.

q13-22.n: Those with a good final abode: patient for Allah, generous, and repelling evil with good.

q14-34.n: Allah's blessings are beyond counting; focusing only on what is missing wrongs oneself.

q15-88.n: Do not fix your eyes on what others have; comparison steals contentment.

q16-18.n: With so many blessings, Allah is forgiving and merciful toward our shortfall in thanks.

q16-53.n: Every blessing is from Allah; people turn to Him in hardship, so they should not forget Him in ease.

q16-91.n: Keeping promises is worship; oaths are not broken after they are confirmed.

q16-128.n: Allah is with the mindful and those who do good; that is support enough.

q17-11.n: People are hasty and may pray against themselves in distress; slow down.

q17-37.n: Humility: you will never split the earth or reach the mountains in height.

q17-70.n: Human dignity is fixed by Allah; no one can take it away.

q17-80.n: A prayer for every beginning and ending: that your entering and leaving be in truth, with support from Allah.

q17-84.n: Everyone acts in their own way; Allah knows best who is better guided, so there is no need to force others.

q20-2.n: The Qur'an was not revealed to make you miserable; religion is mercy, not a burden.

q20-114.n: The student's prayer: asking for more knowledge and staying humble about what we do not know.

q21-35.n: Both good and bad are tests; death is a reality that reorders priorities.

q22-46.n: True blindness is blindness of the heart, which is healed by reflection.

q23-1.n: The traits of the successful: humility in prayer, turning from idle talk, chastity; a practical programme for life.

q23-8.n: Guarding trusts and promises is a trait of the successful believers.

q23-96.n: Answer harm with what is better; this does not mean accepting ongoing injustice.

q24-26.n: Good people for good people; revealed to clear ‘A’ishah, it reassures those falsely accused in their honour.

q24-27.n: Seeking permission protects privacy; today it applies to messages and phones too.

q24-28.n: If permission is refused, leave without anger; respecting others' boundaries is purer for you.

q25-72.n: Passing by idle talk with dignity instead of being dragged into it.

q28-77.n: Do not forget your share of this world: balance between ambition, the Hereafter and doing good.

q29-57.n: Death is a shared reality, and the return to Allah gives it meaning.

q29-60.n: So many creatures do not carry their provision yet Allah provides; whoever moves or migrates, Allah provides for them.

q30-22.n: The diversity of languages and colours is a sign of Allah, not a reason for ranking or contempt.

q30-41.n: Corruption on land and sea comes from human deeds; the aim is that people return.

q31-22.n: Submitting to Allah while doing good is the firmest hold a person can grasp.

q31-34.n: No one knows what tomorrow brings; do your part today and leave tomorrow to Allah.

q33-35.n: Men and women are equal in reward and standing with Allah.

q33-41.n: Remembering Allah often ties the whole day to Him, and anxiety eases.

q33-58.n: Harming people for what they did not do is slander and a clear sin.

q35-8.n: Do not destroy yourself with grief over those who are not guided; your part is to convey, guidance is from Allah.

q35-18.n: No one bears another's sin; you answer for your deeds, not your family's mistakes.

q39-9.n: Knowledge raises its owner; the reflective, fearful and hopeful person is not like the heedless.

q39-23.n: Hearts and skins soften to the Qur'an; listening to it treats a hard heart.

q40-55.n: Allah's promise is true; be patient, seek forgiveness and glorify Him, and relief will come.

q41-46.n: Your deeds are for or against yourself; Allah needs nothing from you for Himself.

q42-30.n: Some misfortunes come from our deeds, and Allah pardons much; it is a call to review, not to self-punishment.

q42-36.n: What is with Allah is better and more lasting; worldly enjoyment is temporary.

q43-32.n: Differences in provision are Allah's distribution for a wisdom; people serve one another.

q45-23.n: Following one's whims without restraint blinds insight; desire can become an idol.

q47-7.n: Whoever stands with the truth, Allah makes them firm.

q48-4.n: Tranquility is sent down by Allah; seek it through prayer and remembrance.

q49-9.n: Reconciling those in conflict is a duty, done with justice, not flattery.

q51-56.n: The question “why am I here?” has an answer: servitude to Allah, which includes work, relationships and mercy.

q52-48.n: “You are in Our sight”: you are not alone in your patience; Allah watches over you.

q55-13.n: A recurring question to awaken awareness of blessings.

q57-16.n: A gentle call to whoever has drifted for long: has the time not come?

q58-11.n: Making room in gatherings is courtesy; true elevation comes through faith and knowledge.

q59-19.n: Forgetting Allah ends in forgetting oneself; returning to Him is returning to oneself.

q63-9.n: Being busy with work and children is natural, but it must not crowd out your bond with Allah.

q64-15.n: Wealth and children are a trial; the great reward is with Allah.

q64-16.n: What is asked of you is what you can, not perfection; this verse lifts the weight of perfectionism.

q70-19.n: Anxiety and grasping are human nature; steady prayer treats them.

q73-10.n: Graceful distance: calmly stepping away from a hurtful person, without revenge or wounding.

q75-14.n: A person knows themselves whatever excuses they make; honesty with oneself starts reform.

q84-6.n: Life is toil and effort, but toil with a goal: meeting Allah.

q89-15.n: Abundance is not always honour, and hardship is not humiliation; both are tests.

q90-4.n: Hardship is part of life's nature; difficulty does not mean you took the wrong road.

q92-4.n: Efforts differ; whoever gives and is mindful, Allah eases their way.

q93-6.n: The Prophet reminded of his past: he was an orphan and Allah sheltered him; recall how you were cared for before.

q94-1.n: The opening of the heart and lifting of burdens come from Allah; right after: with hardship comes ease.

q94-7.n: When you finish one task, turn to the next, and direct your longing to Allah.

q95-4.n: People are created in the finest form; your worth does not drop with illness or appearance.

q99-7.n: Nothing is lost: a small good is seen, and so is a small harm.

q102-1.n: Competing for more distracts until life's end; watch what consumes your life.

q104-1.n: Mocking, sneering and backbiting are sins Allah warns against.

q107-1.n: Harshness to orphans, withholding small kindnesses and showing off contradict the truth of religion.

q108-1.n: Revealed when the Prophet was taunted over the loss of his sons: Allah gives abundant good, and the hater is the one cut off.

q110-1.n: At the moment of success: glorify Allah and seek forgiveness instead of pride.

q112-1.n: Pure monotheism frees the heart from attachment to anything else.
